summary: The Lifelong Health Record entry breaks the "authoritative [noun] of/for" pattern used by the preceding four registries…
comment: The Lifelong Health Record entry breaks the "authoritative [noun] of/for" pattern used by the preceding four registries, instead describing itself as a "governed, person-centred capability" — plausibly intentional given its centralised/federated/hybrid flexibility (649–650), but this rationale is not stated. The clause also contains an apparent text artifact ("...central store. person-centred that") that reads as duplicated/incomplete.

public.text: The Lifelong Health Record entry breaks the "authoritative [noun] of/for" pattern used by the preceding four registries, instead describing itself as a "governed, person-centred capability" — plausibly intentional given its centralised/federated/hybrid flexibility (649–650), but this rationale is not stated. The clause also contains an apparent text artifact ("...central store. person-centred that") that reads as duplicated/incomplete.
public.suggestedRevision: Add a brief clause explaining why the Lifelong Health Record is defined differently from the other four (e.g. "unlike the registries above, it is defined as a capability rather than a single store, because implementation may be centralised, federated, or hybrid"); remove or complete the stray "person-centred that" fragment.
